claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution.
Components inside a Pulumi package inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends the strategies in this guide for structuring Git repositories used to publish packages.
Following the repository-structuring practices in this guide improves the reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages an organization builds and consumes.
Link target: Pulumi packages concept page at /docs/iac/concepts/packages/ and components concept page at /docs/iac/concepts/components/ exist.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), and each is versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.
The version of a source-based Pulumi package is the Git tag on its repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Link targets exist: the 'source-based-plugin-packages' anchor on the packaging-components page and the Private Registry concept page at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry requires applying a semver Git tag (for example, `v1.2.3`) to the repository.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The `pulumi package publish` step in a CI/CD pipeline often runs automated tests before publishing.
Link target exists: /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/ page for the `pulumi package publish` command.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Executable-based package releases are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
Link target exists: the 'executable-based-plugin-packages' anchor on the packaging-components page.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; this is Pulumi's recommended practice.
A repository containing multiple Pulumi packages either has to release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
A 1:1 repository-to-package mapping keeps git tags, release artifacts, and version history aligned.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are fine and expected, and the components ship together at the package's version.
Pulumi recommends: define exactly one package per repository, group a cohesive set of components inside that package, and use multiple repositories (one per package) to manage distinct packages.
The importance of the recommended repository-strategy principles grows as an organization's adoption of Pulumi grows.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with the supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The components in the Pulumi Amazon EKS package are almost always used together and tend to evolve together, so a shared semantic version makes sense.
Link target exists: the Amazon EKS package page at https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/.
A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.

The example repository layout places a `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the root with components under a `components/` directory (`EksCluster/`, `EksIam/`) as a valid layout for a single multi-component package.
It is technically possible to use a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, but Pulumi does not recommend this approach.
Bundling all components into one giant package forfeits meaningful semantic versioning, which is how consumers know whether a change is a bug fix, a new feature, or a breaking change.
When unrelated components share a Pulumi package, every release of the package versions every component the same way, regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.

In a package with two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA yields release v1.1.0 (from v1.0.0), and a breaking change to ComponentB then yields release v2.0.0, consistent with semver minor/major bump rules.
Splitting unrelated components across separate, right-sized packages preserves the semver contract and keeps the upgrade story honest for consuming platform teams.
Link target exists: the Publishing packages guide at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
